interpretation: Five hundred unmodified warmed status calls alternate ten blocks of 25 calls per mode against the same installed native identity. Median wall cost is about 0.062 ms force and 0.031 ms auto; thread CPU closely matches wall time in that isolated check.

A separate counting phase, outside timing, observes twenty distribution lookups in twenty force-mode calls and none in twenty automatic-mode calls. This verifies repeated force-only discovery but does not establish its contribution to the 1.366 ms failed HTTP comparison. No product cache change follows.

The new complete on-workload diagnostic retains the original 200 warm requests, five c16/c64 waves and all thirteen gates. It samples every sixteenth background worker compile, capped at 32. Exactly eighteen samples complete without profiling error across 294 worker compiles; all thirteen diagnostic benchmark gates and final containment pass.

Only the selected context-load thread installs the existing thread-specific sys.setprofile helper; no profiler is installed on HTTP/main/foreign threads. Reports retain fixed source labels and numeric clocks/counts, without frames, locals, arguments or callers.

Instrumented self CPU is largest in native_daemon_route._decide; path identity checks, force-only metadata and environment projection also appear. Callback overhead and possible C-level collection are included in self attribution. These rankings do not prove uninstrumented hot-path cost or justify changing validation.

The driver freezes six explicitly listed observer/native inputs, not the complete benchmark/helper tree. The normal fixed cohort has its separate complete frozen inputs. The diagnostic is never a replacement qualification run.

No product code, deadline, lease, estimator, priority, SDK or approval behavior changes. The original distribution relative HTTP result remains failed. Next use sparse function-boundary/collection observations to separate actual Python CPU from profile overhead and native waits before choosing a correction.
